subject: sentences
title: Two-line stories
about: Two-sentence stories and facts with a question about who, what, where, why, what happened first, or what the story is about. This is grade-level comprehension in a size he can hold in his head.
tip: Before he taps, ask him to tell you the story back in his own words.

cards.q: Pam has a pet frog. It can hop and swim. What is Pam's pet?
cards.note: What asks about a thing in the story. The first sentence says it: a pet frog.

cards.q: Sam lost his cap. Then he found it under the bed. Where was the cap?
cards.note: Where asks about a place. The story says he found it under the bed.

cards.q: It is cold today. Meg puts on her coat. Why does Meg put on a coat?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The first sentence gives it: it is cold.

cards.q: Ben planted a seed. Soon a green plant grew. What grew from the seed?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The second sentence says a green plant grew.

cards.q: Tim fed his dog. Then he took it for a walk. What did Tim do first?
cards.note: First asks about order. The first sentence tells what happened first.

cards.q: Jen baked a cake. She gave a slice to her mom. Who got a slice?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. The story says she gave the slice to her mom.

cards.q: Max fell in the mud. He was sad. Why was Max sad?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. What happened first is why he felt sad.

cards.q: Bees live in a hive. They make sweet honey. What do bees make?
cards.note: This one is a fact. The second sentence says bees make honey.

cards.q: A frog starts as an egg. Then it is a tadpole. What comes first?
cards.note: First asks about order. The story says a frog starts as an egg.

cards.q: Sam and Pam went to the beach. They dug in the sand. Where were they?
cards.note: Where asks about a place. The first sentence names it: the beach.

cards.q: The sun went down. Then the moon came up. What came up after the sun went down?
cards.note: After asks about order. First the sun went down, then the moon came up.

cards.q: Deb has a red kite. The wind took it up high. What took the kite up?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The second sentence says the wind took it up.

cards.q: Nat had a bag of grapes. He gave some to Beth. Who gave Beth some grapes?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. Nat had the grapes and gave some to Beth.

cards.q: Spot is a cat. Spot likes to nap in the sun. What is this story about?
cards.note: The topic is who the story is mostly about. The sun is in the story, but the story is about Spot the cat.
